name: @falkenslab/moodle-mcp

tools.name: configure
tools.description: Set this server's configuration for this session: the Moodle site (url; a new one is added to the server's sites and kept, a known one becomes active, see use_site), whether the browser runs without a window (headless), how student tools view and do things (trail) and the browser profile folder (profileDir). It can also narrow the kinds of tools (scopes), the role (role) or access to read only (access) and tighten how others' data reaches you (studentData), never the other way: widening is the person's, in the client's configuration. Each is optional; only those given change. The URL is checked to be a Moodle site. Kept in memory only, but for a new site, which stays among the server's sites. Returns the effective configuration, as server_info.

url.description: The Moodle site's URL, or any page of it (a course URL works: the site is read from it)

headless.description: Run the browser without a window (logging in always shows one)

trail.description: How student tools view and do things: realistic (real pages, human pace; Moodle logs views and completion) or fast

profileDir.description: Absolute folder for the browser profile that keeps the Moodle session; outside the server's folder

scopes.description: Narrow the kinds of tools for this session: a profile (teacher, student, content) or scopes (content, student-data, grading, communication, as-student, browser). Only fewer than now, never more

studentData.description: Tighten how others' data reaches you for this session (block is strictest). Only stricter than now, never looser

role.description: Keep only one role's tools for this session (teacher or student), from all; never back to all

access.description: read: keep only the tools that change nothing in Moodle for this session; never back to write

tools.name: login
tools.description: Make sure there is a Moodle session. If there is one, returns the logged-in user at once. Otherwise opens a browser window at the site's login page and waits until the person logs in there themselves (the server never sees their password), then returns the user. Call it when another tool reports a missing or expired session.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait for the person to log in, in seconds (default 300)

tools.name: logout
tools.description: End the person's Moodle session in the server's browser, so someone else can log in (another account: login opens the window again). Only Moodle's session ends: a single sign-on provider may keep its own and log the same person back in. Only when the person asks.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Tell who the logged-in person is: user id, username, full name, email, language, time zone, first and last access, and the site. With courseId, also their roles in that course and whether they can edit it and grade in it.

courseId.description: A course id (from list_courses) to also get the person's roles and abilities there

tools.name: get_site_info
tools.description: What the Moodle site says about itself: its name, URL, language, how people log in (its own form, guest access, single sign-on providers) and whether it's in maintenance; readable before logging in. With courseId, also the activity and resource types the person can add to that course (none if they can't edit it): take the type for create_activity from here. Moodle shows its version only to administrators, so it isn't given.

courseId.description: A course to list the activity types that can be added to it

tools.name: list_courses
tools.description: List the Moodle courses the logged-in person is enrolled in (as teacher or student), with their ids, names, category, URL, visibility, dates and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's progress: only as a student, in courses with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' progress is in get_completion_report). Filter by dates with classification.

classification.description: Which courses by their dates: "all" (default), "inprogress", "future" or "past"

tools.name: get_course_structure
tools.description: Get a Moodle course's sections and activities: ids, names, types, URLs, visibility, whether the person can open each one, restrictions and, where Moodle tracks it, the person's completion: only as a student, on activities with completion tracking (a teacher gets none; students' completion is in get_completion_report). With details, also each activity's dates and restriction text as the course page shows them. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

details.description: Also read the course page for each activity's dates and restriction text (slower; default false)

tools.name: get_activity_content
tools.description: Read a content activity as a person would, so Moodle logs the view: a page's or label's text, a book's chapters, a URL resource's target, or a file resource's or folder's files (as links). Takes the id and type from get_course_structure. With the realistic trail it reads page by page at a reader's pace and reports progress.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: list_participants
tools.description: List a course's participants with their roles and groups, as the participants page does: people as aliases when the server pseudonymizes, never emails or profile fields. Filter by role, group, or those who haven't accessed the course since a date (inactiveSince). A page at a time: limit participants (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

role.description: Only this role's, by its id (as the participants' roles give it)

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

inactiveSince.description: Only those who haven't accessed the course since this date (ISO 8601)

limit.description: How many participants (50 by default, up to 500)

offset.description: How many participants to skip first (0 by default)

tools.name: list_groups
tools.description: List the groups of a course the person can see, with their members (as aliases when the server pseudonymizes). Their ids are what the reports' group filter takes.

tools.name: list_potential_users
tools.description: Find users the person may enrol in a course by manual enrolment, as the "Enrol users" dialog does: matching search in their name or the identity fields the site shows (up to 100 when empty). People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes, never their emails. Enrol them with enrol_users.

search.description: Part of a name, an email, an ID number…

tools.name: enrol_users
tools.description: Enrol users in a course by manual enrolment, as the "Enrol users" dialog does: with a role (the enrolment's default unless roleId), from start (now) until end (the enrolment's default duration). Takes them as list_potential_users gives them. Those already enrolled keep their enrolment, with the new dates. Confirm with the person first.

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

roleId.description: The role to give, as list_participants' roles give it

tools.name: unenrol_user
tools.description: Unenrol someone from a course: removes every enrolment of theirs the person may remove, with their roles and group memberships in the course; removed and kept name the enrolment methods. Their work in the course stays in Moodle but they lose access. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: set_user_roles
tools.description: Set a participant's roles in a course, as the participants page's roles column does: gives the roles in roleIds the person may assign and takes away the other ones they may assign; roles from elsewhere stay. Returns the roles afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

roleIds.description: Role ids, as list_participants' roles give them

tools.name: set_group_members
tools.description: Add and remove members of a group, as its members page does: only the course's participants can be added. Takes them as list_participants gives them: aliases (add, remove) when the server pseudonymizes, else user ids (addIds, removeIds). Returns the members afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

add.description: Aliases to add, when the server pseudonymizes

remove.description: Aliases to remove, when the server pseudonymizes

addIds.description: User ids to add, when the server shows names

removeIds.description: User ids to remove, when the server shows names

tools.name: create_group
tools.description: Create a group in a course with Moodle's group form. Add its members with set_group_members. Returns its id. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

enrolmentKey.description: A key that enrols students straight into this group with self enrolment

tools.name: update_group
tools.description: Change a group's name, description, ID number or enrolment key; what isn't given stays. Confirm with the person first.

groupId.description: The group's id, as list_groups gives it

enrolmentKey.description: A key that enrols students straight into this group with self enrolment

tools.name: delete_group
tools.description: Delete a group; its members stay in the course. Activities set to work by groups lose it. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

groupId.description: The group's id, as list_groups gives it

tools.name: list_groupings
tools.description: List a course's groupings (sets of groups an activity can be limited to) with their groups' ids. Needs the right to manage groups.

tools.name: create_grouping
tools.description: Create a grouping in a course with Moodle's form; give it its groups with set_grouping_groups. Returns its id. Confirm with the person first.

tools.name: delete_grouping
tools.description: Delete a grouping; its groups stay. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

groupingId.description: The grouping's id, as list_groupings gives it

tools.name: set_grouping_groups
tools.description: Make a grouping's groups exactly groupIds, adding and removing as its page does; groups of other courses are left out and named. Returns its groups afterwards. Confirm with the person first.

groupingId.description: The grouping's id, as list_groupings gives it

tools.name: list_enrolment_methods
tools.description: List how people can enrol in a course, in the order Moodle tries them: each method's type, name, whether it's on, how many it enrolled, the role it gives and, for self enrolment and guest access, whether it asks for a key (never the key), dates and limit.

tools.name: set_enrolment_method
tools.description: Change an enrolment method with its form, by its id or the course's first of a type (methodType "self": added when the course has none and Moodle offers it): turn it on or off, its key, dates, role, limit and welcome message. Only what's given changes. Returns the method afterwards (never the key). Opens or closes the course to people: confirm with the person first.

methodType.description: Or the method's type, such as "self" or "guest"

key.description: Self enrolment or guest access key; empty to remove it

start.description: From when, ISO 8601; "none" to remove it

end.description: Until when, ISO 8601; "none" to remove it

welcomeMessage.description: Self enrolment: send this welcome message

noWelcome.description: Self enrolment: send no welcome message

tools.name: get_grader_report
tools.description: Read everyone's grades in a course as the grader report shows them, in one group when given: its columns (grade items, categories, the course total) and a row per participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes) with their grades.

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

tools.name: get_completion_report
tools.description: Read a course's progress report: every participant's completion (an alias when the server pseudonymizes) of every activity that tracks it, in one group when given; whether it's manual or automatic, and whether a teacher overrode it.

group.description: Only this group's members, by its id from list_groups

tools.name: get_activity_report
tools.description: Read a course's activity report: per activity, how many times it was viewed, by how many people and when last, from the logs (between from and until when given). Counts only, no one's name. Activities nobody viewed come with zero.

tools.name: get_participation_report
tools.description: Read an activity's participation report: everyone with a role (all the roles it offers, unless roleId) and how many actions they made there (views or posts only with action; since a date with since); those who did nothing come with 0. People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes.

tools.name: get_course_logs
tools.description: Read a course's logs, newest first, as its logs report lists them: by a user (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), an activity, a kind of action and a time span, a page at a time: limit entries (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Each entry: when, who, who it was about, where, what happened (Moodle's longer description only with includeDescriptions). Never IP addresses.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

offset.description: How many entries to skip first, newest first (0 by default)

includeDescriptions.description: Also each entry's description, Moodle's sentence about it (longer; default false)

tools.name: set_grade
tools.description: Set a participant's grade in a grade item, as the gradebook's single view does: a manual item takes it; an activity's or a category's is overridden (until override false takes it off). Also feedback and excluding it from the totals. The grade as text: points ("7.5"), a scale item, or "none" to empty it. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

itemId.description: The grade item, as get_gradebook_setup or get_grader_report gives it

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

feedback.description: No aliases in it, since the student reads it

override.description: false: take an activity's or category's override off

tools.name: export_grades
tools.description: Save a course's grades into a local folder as Moodle exports them for a teacher: a spreadsheet (xlsx, ods), CSV or XML, with the items, group, display and feedback chosen. The file names every participant: only with names in clear (the server's student data level), since a file can't be pseudonymized.

tools.name: override_completion
tools.description: Set a participant's completion of an activity as a teacher does from the progress report (an override, shown as such). Takes the participant as get_completion_report gives them. Returns the state saved. Changes the participant's progress: confirm with the person first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id)

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: list_assignments
tools.description: List the assignments of a Moodle course: their ids (course module ids, for the other assignment tools), names, URLs, visibility and section. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: get_submissions
tools.description: Get the participants' submissions to a Moodle assignment, a page at a time (limit participants, 25 by default, after skipping offset; more says whether there are others): who (an alias when the server pseudonymizes, else id and name), status (submitted; draft; new: a submission started but nothing in it yet; reopened; none: no submission at all), whether it needs grading, extensions, the participant's dates and, by default, the content (online text and file links; names and contact data in it redacted when pseudonymizing). Changes nothing, but Moodle logs it as the teacher viewing the grading pages, as it does for its own grader. Takes the assignment id from list_assignments.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (its course module id), as list_assignments gives it

includeContent.description: Include each submission's content: online text and file links (default true)

limit.description: How many participants (25 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many participants to skip first, in the grading table's order (0 by default)

tools.name: list_discussions
tools.description: List the discussions of a Moodle forum: subject, who started it and when, the last post's author and time, the number of replies (0: unanswered) and whether it's locked. A page at a time: limit discussions (30 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Takes the forum id from get_course_structure; read one with get_discussion.

forumId.description: The forum's id (its course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

limit.description: How many discussions (30 by default, up to 100)

offset.description: How many discussions to skip first, in the forum's order (0 by default)

tools.name: get_discussion
tools.description: Read a Moodle forum discussion's posts, oldest first, a page at a time (limit posts, 50 by default, after skipping offset; more says whether there are others): author (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), time, the post it replies to, the message as plain text (names and contact data redacted when pseudonymizing) and attachments. Takes the discussion id from list_discussions.

discussionId.description: The discussion id, as list_discussions gives it

limit.description: How many posts (50 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many posts to skip first, oldest first (0 by default)

tools.name: get_my_grades
tools.description: Get the logged-in person's grade report for a course: each grade item (with its activity id), category and the course total, with grade, range, percentage, weight, letter, feedback and contribution, as Moodle shows them. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Save a file of the Moodle site to a local folder, with the person's session: a resource's or folder's file (get_activity_content), an assignment's brief file or submitted file (get_assignment, get_submissions), a forum attachment (get_discussion). Only URLs of the configured site's host (its media too: videos it serves outside Moodle); external links (YouTube…) are for other tools. Never overwrites: an existing name gets a number. Returns where it was saved.

url.description: The file's URL on the site, as the other tools give it (…/pluginfile.php/…)

destDir.description: Absolute local folder to save into; created if missing

tools.name: get_survey
tools.description: Read a survey (the questionnaire plugin, or Moodle's feedback) as the person: whether they can answer it now, its messages (completed, closed…), and every question on every page, with whether it's required and its fields (names, options).

activityId.description: The survey's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: submit_survey
tools.description: Answer a survey and submit it, page by page as its form goes: responses maps field names (from get_survey) to values ("1"/"0" for checkboxes, an option's value for choices and selects, text otherwise). Every name is checked first; Moodle's complaints (a required question left out) come back by page. Usually one response per person: confirm the answers with the person first, and ask them for personal data instead of guessing.

activityId.description: The survey's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: The activity's type, as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_choice
tools.description: Read a choice activity (a poll) as the person sees it: its question, the options with their ids, whether it's open, whether several can be chosen and whether the answer can change, and the person's answer.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: answer_choice
tools.description: Answer a choice activity as the person, with one option (several where the choice allows them) by id from get_choice, as "Save my choice" does. Returns the choice afterwards. Answers as the person, and some choices don't allow changing it: confirm with the person first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_lesson_page
tools.description: Read the page of a lesson the person is on (starting the lesson the first time): a content page with its buttons, a question with its fields, or the end with the score. Answer it with answer_lesson_page.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: answer_lesson_page
tools.description: Go on in a lesson as the person: press a content page's button (by its label, or by its position from 1), or answer a question page's fields by name (an option's value for choice and select, text for text). Returns Moodle's feedback, if any, and the next page; reaching the end ends the attempt. Answers count towards the lesson's grade and can't be taken back. With the realistic trail it pauses to read the page first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

button.description: A content page's button, by its label

responses.description: A question page's answers: field name → value, as get_lesson_page gives the fields

tools.name: get_h5p_activity
tools.description: Read an H5P activity: its content type (the H5P library), whether Moodle tracks attempts, and the person's own attempts with their scores. Solving the content itself (it runs in a player) is for the browser fallback tools.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_scorm
tools.description: Read a SCORM activity as the person sees it: attempts allowed and made, grading method, the grade reported and each attempt's, and its SCOs (the package's parts) with the person's status and score in the last attempt. Use it before open_scorm, and after doing the package to see what Moodle recorded.

activityId.description: The SCORM activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: open_scorm
tools.description: Open a SCORM activity in Moodle's player, as the person, in the browser tools' tab: the last attempt continues unless newAttempt, at the first SCO unless scoId. Opening it starts an attempt in Moodle. Then do the package with the browser tools: browser_snapshot reads it (refs inside its frame start with f, like f2e9), browser_click, browser_type and browser_select act on them, browser_wait waits for its texts. Afterwards, check the result with get_scorm instead of assuming it. Nothing marks a SCORM done or graded but doing it.

activityId.description: The SCORM activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

scoId.description: The SCO to open, as get_scorm gives it; the first when missing

newAttempt.description: Start a new attempt instead of continuing the last one

tools.name: set_completion
tools.description: Mark the person's own completion of an activity with manual completion, done or not done, as its "Mark as done" button does. Activities that complete on their own (by viewing, grade, submission) can't be marked: Moodle says so. Doing it twice changes nothing.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: list_pending
tools.description: List what the logged-in person still has to do in a course: activities whose completion is tracked and not complete or, where completion isn't tracked, graded activities without a grade yet; with their dates, restrictions and whether they can be opened now. Takes the course id from list_courses.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

tools.name: get_activities_overview
tools.description: Moodle's activities overview of a course, as the person sees it: per activity, its columns (due date, submissions, what needs grading, attempts, the person's own grade, forum subscriptions…), by type or for every type in the course. For a teacher, the quickest way to see what's waiting to be graded (alert "Needs grading"); for a student, what's due and their results. Moodle 5 and later.

type.description: One activity type (assign, quiz, forum…; "resource" for every resource type); every type when missing

tools.name: list_deadlines
tools.description: What the person has to do by a date, from Moodle's calendar (submit an assignment, attempt a quiz…), in one course or all of them: from a week ago (overdue ones) to some days ahead. Each with its activity id, date, whether it's overdue and the action Moodle offers. Teachers get few such events: for what's waiting to be graded, use get_activities_overview.

courseId.description: One course; every course when missing

tools.name: get_course_updates
tools.description: What changed in a course's activities since a date (settings, content files, forum posts, submissions, attempts, grades…), as Moodle tracks it for the person, with each activity's name and type. Useful at the start of a session: what's new since last time.

since.description: ISO date and time; a week ago when missing

tools.name: get_quiz_info
tools.description: Read a quiz's page as the person: description, its rules (attempts allowed, grading method, time limit…), dates, overall feedback, the person's attempts (with their ids, in progress or finished, and grades) and whether they can start one now.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: start_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Start an attempt at a quiz, or continue the one in progress, as the quiz page's button does; returns the attempt's id and its questions with their fields and options. Starting uses up one of the attempts allowed, and a time limit starts running: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: get_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Read every question of an attempt in progress, page by page: text, images, fields with their options, and the answers saved so far.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: answer_quiz_questions
tools.description: Save answers in an attempt in progress, as the attempt's pages do; it doesn't finish the attempt. Each answer names a question's slot and its fields by name with the value to give: an option's value for choice and select fields, "1" or "0" for checkboxes, text for text fields. Returns the questions with their saved answers. With the realistic trail it pauses to read each page first.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

responses.description: Field name → value, as get_quiz_attempt gives the fields

tools.name: finish_quiz_attempt
tools.description: Submit an attempt for grading, as "Submit all and finish" does: no answer can change afterwards. Returns the review when the quiz shows it. Final: confirm with the person first, after checking the answers with get_quiz_attempt.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: get_attempt_review
tools.description: Read a finished attempt's review, as far as the quiz shows it: status, marks and grade, and per question whether it was right, the mark, feedback and the right answer. Someone else's attempt (a teacher's view) names them by alias, and their written answers are redacted, when the server pseudonymizes.

attemptId.description: The attempt's id, as start_quiz_attempt or get_quiz_info gives it

tools.name: get_quiz_results
tools.description: Read a quiz's attempts as its grades report shows them: per attempt the participant (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), state, dates, grade and the mark per question; with responses, also each answer given (redacted when pseudonymizing). A page at a time: limit attempts (50 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

responses.description: Also the answer per question (default false)

limit.description: How many attempts (50 by default, up to 500)

offset.description: How many attempts to skip first, in the report's order (0 by default)

tools.name: set_quiz_override
tools.description: Give a participant their own quiz settings, as the quiz's user overrides do: open and close dates, time limit in minutes, or number of attempts (0 unlimited); what isn't given stays the quiz's. Takes the participant as list_participants gives them. Confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: list_questions_to_grade
tools.description: List a quiz's questions that wait for grading by hand (essays…), each with how many to grade and the finished attempts whose answer needs it (by attempt id, with the participant as an alias when the server pseudonymizes). Read an answer with get_attempt_review; grade it with grade_quiz_question.

tools.name: grade_quiz_question
tools.description: Grade one question of a finished attempt by hand, with a comment, as the review's "Make comment or override mark" does: an essay waiting for grading, or any question whose mark is overridden. The mark is in the question's points (0 to its maximum). Returns the attempt's grade afterwards when shown. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

comment.description: No aliases in it, since the student reads it

tools.name: get_assignment
tools.description: Read an assignment as the logged-in student sees it: the brief and its files, dates, the submission's status and content, grade and feedback, and whether it can be edited or submitted now.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: save_submission
tools.description: Save the logged-in student's submission to an assignment: its online text (HTML, replacing what was there) and files to add (absolute local paths). Doesn't submit it for grading when the assignment asks students to click submit: submit_assignment does. Returns the assignment as the student sees it. Changes the submission: confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: submit_assignment
tools.description: Submit the saved submission for grading: it can't be changed afterwards unless the teacher reopens it. When the site asks to accept a statement (it's your own work…), the call fails quoting it until acceptStatement is true. Final: confirm with the person first, after checking the submission with get_assignment.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

acceptStatement.description: The person accepts the site's submission statement

tools.name: get_rubric
tools.description: Read how an assignment is graded: simple (a grade or a scale), a rubric (criteria with their levels and scores) or a marking guide (criteria with their maximum score). The criterion and level ids are what grade_submission's fields take. Takes the assignment id from list_assignments; needs at least one participant.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

tools.name: grade_submission
tools.description: Grade a participant in an assignment, as Moodle's grader does: a grade (simple grading), a rubric's levels or a marking guide's scores per criterion (ids from get_rubric) with remarks, feedback comments (HTML, when the assignment has them on), whether to notify the student, and any other grading field by name in fields. Takes the participant as get_submissions gives them: user (an alias) when the server pseudonymizes, else userId. Works with or without a submission. Returns the grade saved. Changes grades students may see: confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

grade.description: The grade as text: a number within the range ("7.5"), or a scale item

feedback.description: Feedback comments (HTML); no aliases in it, since the student reads it

notify.description: Notify the student; Moodle's default when missing

rubric.description: A rubric's level per criterion: criterion id → level id, as get_rubric gives them

guide.description: A marking guide's score per criterion: criterion id → score

remarks.description: Remarks per criterion of a rubric or guide: criterion id → text; no aliases

feedbackFiles.description: Absolute local paths of feedback files to return to the student

workflowState.description: With the marking workflow on: the state to leave the submission in ("released" shows the student the grade)

applyToGroup.description: In a group assignment: give the same grade and feedback to the whole group

fields.description: Other grading form fields by name, e.g. a rubric's levels

tools.name: grant_extension
tools.description: Grant participants an extension of an assignment's due date until a date, as the assignment's extension form does (several at once). Takes them as get_submissions gives them: users (aliases) when the server pseudonymizes, else userIds. Moodle refuses a date before the due date. Confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

tools.name: set_workflow_state
tools.description: Set the marking workflow state of participants' submissions, as the grading table's bulk action does: "released" shows them their grades (notify tells them). Takes them as get_submissions gives them. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

tools.name: allocate_marker
tools.description: Allocate a marker (someone who can grade; several where the assignment uses several per submission) to participants' submissions, as the grading table's bulk action does; Moodle leaves submissions past marking alone. Participants and markers as get_submissions gives them: aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Confirm with the person first.

assignmentId.description: The assignment's id (course module id), as list_assignments gives it

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

markers.description: The markers' aliases, when the server pseudonymizes

markerIds.description: The markers' user ids, when the server shows names

tools.name: reply_to_post
tools.description: Reply to a post in a Moodle forum discussion, with optional attachments (local files). The subject defaults to Moodle's "Re: …". Returns the new post's id and its discussion. Posts as the person, visibly: confirm the text with the person first.

postId.description: The post to reply to, as get_discussion gives it

message.description: The message (HTML); no aliases in it, since people read it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

subscribe.description: Subscribe to the discussion; Moodle's default when missing

fields.description: Other post form fields by name, e.g. {"pinned": true} for a teacher

tools.name: create_discussion
tools.description: Start a discussion in a Moodle forum, with optional attachments and embedded images (local files); a teacher can post announcements this way in the announcements forum. Returns the new discussion's id, and whether it's pinned and the person subscribed, read back. Posts as the person, visibly: confirm the text with the person first.

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

message.description: The message (HTML); no aliases in it, since people read it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

subscribe.description: Subscribe to the discussion; Moodle's default when missing

fields.description: Other post form fields by name, e.g. {"pinned": true} for a teacher

tools.name: set_discussion_state
tools.description: Pin or unpin, lock or unlock a forum discussion, as the discussion list's menu does; what's already so is left alone. Returns the discussion as the forum lists it afterwards. Students see it: confirm with the person first.

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: set_discussion_subscription
tools.description: Subscribe the person to a forum discussion, or unsubscribe them, as the discussion list's toggle does: Moodle then emails them its new posts. What's already so is left alone. Returns the discussion as the forum lists it afterwards.

forumId.description: The forum's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: edit_post
tools.description: Change a forum post through Moodle's own form, as its author (within the site's editing time) or a moderator: its subject, message (HTML), and attachments to add or remove. Only what's given changes. Returns the post afterwards (its author as an alias when the server pseudonymizes). Visible to the forum: confirm with the person first.

message.description: HTML; no aliases in it, since people read it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Delete a forum post and its replies through Moodle's own confirmation; a discussion's first post takes the whole discussion. Only a moderator deletes someone else's post or one with replies. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: get_forum_grades
tools.description: Read the whole-forum grades of a forum graded as a whole, as its grader shows them: one per person it can grade (aliases when the server pseudonymizes), with how it's graded (points or scale) and who graded.

tools.name: grade_forum_user
tools.description: Give a participant their whole-forum grade, as the forum's grader does: points ("7"), a scale item, or "none" to take it away; notify sends them Moodle's notification. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: rate
tools.description: Rate a forum post, a glossary entry or a database record as the person, as the rating menu under it does: a scale item's name, or a number (a point scale's points); "none" takes the person's rating away. Returns the item's aggregate afterwards. Students may see it: confirm with the person first.

itemId.description: The post's, entry's or record's id

discussionId.description: For a forum post: its discussion

tools.name: get_workshop
tools.description: Read a workshop's phase and its report as a teacher sees it: every submission (author, title, grade once calculated) and every assessment (reviewer, the submission's author, the grade it gives, its weight, the grade for assessing). People as aliases when the server pseudonymizes. Empty lists before the submission phase, or for someone who can't see every submission.

tools.name: set_workshop_phase
tools.description: Switch a workshop to a phase (setup, submission, assessment, evaluation, closed), forwards or back, as its page's phase links do. Moodle allocates nothing and calculates no grades on its own when it switches. Changes what students can do: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: assess_workshop_submission
tools.description: Assess a workshop submission as the person, through the workshop's assessment form (its grading strategy's): a grade and comment per criterion in the form's order, overall feedback for the author (HTML), and any other field by name. A new assessment the first time, the same one changed after. Only in the assessment phase. Returns the grade it gives. The author reads it: confirm with the person first.

feedback.description: Overall feedback for the author (HTML); no aliases in it

fields.description: Any other field of the form, by name

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description: List the person's notifications, newest first (only unread ones when asked), a page at a time: limit of them (30 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others to ask for with a bigger offset. Each: subject, text, who it's from (an alias when the server pseudonymizes), when, whether it's read, and where it leads. Names in the texts are redacted when pseudonymizing.

offset.description: How many to skip first, newest first (0 by default); with unreadOnly, it counts unread ones

tools.name: mark_notifications_read
tools.description: Mark all the person's notifications read, as the notifications popover's "Mark all as read" does. Doing it twice changes nothing.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List the person's message conversations, latest first: private, group or with themselves, their members (aliases when the server pseudonymizes), unread count and the last message as text. A page at a time: limit conversations (20 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Read one with get_conversation.

limit.description: How many conversations (20 by default, up to 100)

offset.description: How many conversations to skip first, latest first (0 by default)

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Read a message conversation: its members and each message's sender (aliases when the server pseudonymizes), text and time; names and contact data in the texts are redacted when pseudonymizing. A page at a time, counted from the newest: limit messages (50 by default) after skipping offset, the first page the latest, each page's messages oldest first; more says whether there are older ones. Takes the id from list_conversations.

limit.description: How many messages (50 by default, up to 200)

offset.description: How many messages to skip first, counted from the newest (0 by default)

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a private message to someone, as the messaging drawer does: to user (an alias) when the server pseudonymizes, else userId. The text is plain; no aliases in it, since the recipient reads it. Returns the message and its conversation. Sent as the person, visibly: confirm the text and the recipient with the person first.

user.description: The participant's alias, as the reading tools give it when the server pseudonymizes

userId.description: The participant's user id, when the server shows names

tools.name: message_participants
tools.description: Send one private message to several participants of a course, as the participants page's "Send a message" does: to users (aliases) or userIds, or to everyone chosen by role, group or inactiveSince (everyone when none is given), the person left out. Returns who got it and who Moodle didn't write to, and why. The text is plain, with no aliases in it. Sent as the person, visibly: confirm the text and the recipients with the person first.

users.description: The participants' aliases, as the reading tools give them when the server pseudonymizes

userIds.description: The participants' user ids, when the server shows names

inactiveSince.description: Or: everyone who hasn't accessed the course since this date (ISO 8601)

tools.name: create_activity
tools.description: Create an activity or resource of any type (page, label, url, resource, folder, assign, quiz, forum…) at the end of a section, through Moodle's own form, hidden from students by default. Common fields have their own inputs, access restrictions and completion included; any other setting goes in settings by its form field name. files are local paths uploaded to a file resource or folder, or a SCORM's package (type scorm, the first file). Returns the new activity's id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

sectionId.description: The section's id, as get_course_structure gives it

type.description: Moodle's module name: page, label, url, resource, folder, assign, quiz, forum, book…

files.description: Absolute local paths: a file resource's file (the first is the main one), a folder's files, a SCORM's package (.zip)

description.description: The description (HTML), shown on the activity's page

content.description: A page's content, or a label's text (HTML)

visibility.description: "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link, where the site allows it

restrictions.description: When students can open it ({ conditions: [] } removes them)

type.description: "date": between from and until; "grade": a grade in activityId between min and max (percent); "completion": activityId in state; "group": a member of groupId; "other": a condition only Moodle's JSON can say

activityId.description: grade, completion: the activity (course module id)

min.description: grade: the lowest grade, in percent

state.description: completion: the state the activity must be in

groupId.description: group: the group, as list_groups gives it

json.description: other: Moodle's availability JSON for this condition, as read

hidden.description: While not met: hidden from students, instead of shown greyed out with the conditions

tracking.description: "none": not tracked; "manual": the student marks it; "conditions": the ones below

expected.description: The completion date shown to students, ISO 8601

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

settings.description: Any other form field by its name in Moodle's activity form, e.g. {"duedate[enabled]": true, "duedate[day]": 12, "grade[modgrade_point]": 10}

tools.name: update_activity
tools.description: Change an existing activity through Moodle's own form: name, description, a page's or label's content, a URL's target, visibility, access restrictions, completion, a file resource's or folder's files (add, remove by their path as get_activity_settings lists them, or replace all), or any other setting by its form field name in settings. Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

description.description: The description (HTML), shown on the activity's page

content.description: A page's content, or a label's text (HTML)

visibility.description: "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link, where the site allows it

restrictions.description: When students can open it ({ conditions: [] } removes them)

type.description: "date": between from and until; "grade": a grade in activityId between min and max (percent); "completion": activityId in state; "group": a member of groupId; "other": a condition only Moodle's JSON can say

activityId.description: grade, completion: the activity (course module id)

min.description: grade: the lowest grade, in percent

state.description: completion: the state the activity must be in

groupId.description: group: the group, as list_groups gives it

json.description: other: Moodle's availability JSON for this condition, as read

hidden.description: While not met: hidden from students, instead of shown greyed out with the conditions

tracking.description: "none": not tracked; "manual": the student marks it; "conditions": the ones below

expected.description: The completion date shown to students, ISO 8601

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

settings.description: Any other form field by its name in Moodle's activity form, e.g. {"duedate[enabled]": true, "duedate[day]": 12, "grade[modgrade_point]": 10}

files.description: A file resource's or folder's files; untouched when missing

remove.description: Paths in the activity, as get_activity_settings lists its files

replace.description: Absolute local paths that become all its files

tools.name: get_activity_settings
tools.description: Read every setting of an activity as its edit form holds them, without changing anything: its module, name, description, each field with its form name, label, value and options, a resource's, folder's or SCORM's files, and its access restrictions and completion in the terms update_activity takes. Use it before update_activity. Teachers only. Takes the activity id from get_course_structure.

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: edit_activity
tools.description: Move an activity to another section (at its end) or before another activity, to reorder a course; rename it; or set its visibility ("shown", "hidden", or "stealth": hidden from the course page but available by link). Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

sectionId.description: Move it to the end of this section

beforeActivityId.description: Move it before this activity (in that activity's section)

tools.name: duplicate_activity
tools.description: Duplicate an activity right after itself, with its settings and content (not participants' data). Returns the copy's id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: delete_activity
tools.description: Delete an activity from a course, with its participants' data (submissions, attempts, posts, grades). Destructive: confirm with the person first, naming the activity.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

activityId.description: The activity's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: add_section
tools.description: Add a section to a course, at the end or after a given section, optionally named and described. Returns its id and the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

afterSectionId.description: Add it after this section; at the end when missing

tools.name: edit_section
tools.description: Change a section: rename it, describe it, show or hide it (with its activities), restrict access to it, or move it after another section. Only what is given changes. Returns the course structure. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

sectionId.description: A section's id (not its number), as get_course_structure gives it

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

restrictions.description: When students can open it ({ conditions: [] } removes them)

type.description: "date": between from and until; "grade": a grade in activityId between min and max (percent); "completion": activityId in state; "group": a member of groupId; "other": a condition only Moodle's JSON can say

activityId.description: grade, completion: the activity (course module id)

min.description: grade: the lowest grade, in percent

state.description: completion: the state the activity must be in

groupId.description: group: the group, as list_groups gives it

json.description: other: Moodle's availability JSON for this condition, as read

hidden.description: While not met: hidden from students, instead of shown greyed out with the conditions

tools.name: delete_section
tools.description: Delete a section and every activity in it, with their participants' data. Destructive: confirm with the person first, saying which activities go with it.

courseId.description: The course's id, as list_courses gives it

sectionId.description: A section's id (not its number), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: update_course
tools.description: Change a course's full name, short name, summary (HTML) or any other setting by its field name in Moodle's course settings form (settings), through that form. Only what is given changes. Returns the course afterwards. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

embed.description: Absolute local files (images…) to embed in the HTML, which names each by its file name:

settings.description: Other fields by their name in the course settings form, e.g. {"visible": 0, "startdate[day]": 1}

tools.name: copy_course
tools.description: Copy a course into a new one, as Moodle's "Copy course" does: its content (and, with withUsers, its people's enrolments and data) under a new full and short name, in a category (the course's unless given), with new dates. Needs the rights to back up, restore and create courses. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Creates a course: confirm with the person first.

withUsers.description: Also its participants and their data (default false)

tools.name: backup_course
tools.description: Back a course up to a .mbz file in a local folder, through Moodle's backup wizard: its content, and with withUsers its people's data too (anonymize makes their names anonymous). Or only some of it: sections (each with everything in it) and activities, never with people's data, and the file naming no one and no site unless anonymous is false. Moodle keeps a copy in the course's backup area. Restore it with restore_course, on this site or another. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten.

destDir.description: An absolute local folder for the file

anonymize.description: With users: Moodle makes their names and contact data anonymous

sections.description: Only these sections, by id (get_course_structure), each with everything in it

activities.description: Only these activities and resources, by course module id

anonymous.description: The file names no person and no site or course of origin: true by default for sections or activities, false for a whole course

tools.name: restore_course
tools.description: Restore a .mbz backup through Moodle's restore wizard: into a new course in a category (no intoCourseId), or into an existing course, adding to its content (mode merge, the default) or replacing it (replace deletes the course's content first). Merged into a course, sectionId puts every restored activity at the end of that section, and afterSectionId the backup's sections as new ones after that one; the result names the new sections and activities, and warnings what was left broken (restrictions or links to what wasn't restored) for the person to fix. A new course takes the backup's names unless fullName and shortName are given. A backup from a newer Moodle, or with activity types this site doesn't offer, is refused. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Changes Moodle, and replace can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

intoCourseId.description: An existing course to restore into; a new course when missing

categoryId.description: For a new course: its category

mode.description: Into an existing course: add to it (default) or replace its content

withUsers.description: Restore the participants' data the backup has (default false)

sectionId.description: Merged into a course: every restored activity at the end of this section

afterSectionId.description: Merged into a course: the backup's sections as new sections after this one

tools.name: import_activities
tools.description: Import activities from another course into a course, as Moodle's "Import" does: all of them, or only activityIds, with their sections, never people's data. Returns the new activities' ids. It can take minutes: Moodle does it in steps, and waits up to ten. Changes the course: confirm with the person first.

activityIds.description: Only these activities of the other course (course module ids)

tools.name: reset_course
tools.description: Reset a course as Moodle's reset form does: delete only what's named in delete (submissions, attempts, posts, grades… in every activity that has them), unenrol the people with unenrolRoles, move the start date (and the activities' dates with it), and set any other field of the form by name. Nothing is deleted unless named. Can't be undone: confirm every item with the person first. Returns Moodle's report.

unenrolRoles.description: Role ids whose people are unenrolled

fields.description: Any other field of the reset form, by name

tools.name: list_question_banks
tools.description: List the question banks of a course: its shared banks (usable by any quiz in the course) and the activities' own banks (a quiz's, usable only there). Returns their ids, which list_questions, import_questions and create_question take.

tools.name: list_questions
tools.description: List a question bank's categories and the questions in them, category by category: id, name, type, status and category. A page at a time: limit questions (100 by default) after skipping offset; more says whether there are others. Takes the bank id from list_question_banks.

bankId.description: The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it

limit.description: How many questions (100 by default, up to 1000)

offset.description: How many questions to skip first, category by category (0 by default)

tools.name: import_questions
tools.description: Import questions into a question bank from GIFT or Moodle XML, given as text or as a local file, through the bank's import form: the way to add several at once. Moodle checks the whole file first: when it can't parse it, nothing is imported and its messages come back. Returns the questions created. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

bankId.description: The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it

file.description: Or an absolute path to a local file in that format

categoryId.description: The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing

tools.name: create_question
tools.description: Create one question in a question bank through its type's form: multichoice, truefalse, shortanswer, numerical or essay. For several, import_questions is faster. Returns the new question's id. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

bankId.description: The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it

fraction.description: Its share of the mark: 1 right, 0 wrong, negatives as penalties (the nearest one Moodle offers)

categoryId.description: The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing

fields.description: Any other field of the type's form, by name

tools.name: update_question
tools.description: Change a question of a bank through its type's form: only what's given changes (answers replaces them all). Saving makes a new version with its own id, the one returned, which quizzes using the latest version get from then on. Changes the bank: confirm with the person first.

bankId.description: The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it

fraction.description: Its share of the mark: 1 right, 0 wrong, negatives as penalties (the nearest one Moodle offers)

categoryId.description: The bank category, as list_questions gives it; the bank's default when missing

fields.description: Any other field of the type's form, by name

tools.name: delete_questions
tools.description: Delete questions from a bank, every version of each, as the bank's delete action does. Moodle doesn't delete a question a quiz uses: it hides it, and hidden lists those. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

bankId.description: The bank's id (a course module id), as list_question_banks gives it

tools.name: set_question_status
tools.description: Set a bank question ready (quizzes can use it) or draft, as the bank's status menu does.

tools.name: get_quiz_structure
tools.description: List a quiz's questions as its edit page does, in order: each slot's page, question id, type (or random), name and mark. Teachers only.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

tools.name: add_questions_to_quiz
tools.description: Add questions to a quiz: bank questions by id (from list_questions) and/or random questions from a bank category, at the end or on a given page. A quiz that has been attempted can't change its questions: Moodle refuses. Returns the quiz's structure afterwards. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

questionIds.description: Bank questions, as list_questions gives them

random.description: Random questions drawn from a category

categoryId.description: The bank category, as list_questions gives it

page.description: The page to add them to; the last when missing

tools.name: edit_quiz_slot
tools.description: Change one slot of a quiz: its maximum mark, and where it is (after another slot, 0 for first, and on a page), as the edit page does. After attempts, Moodle lets the mark change (it regrades them) but not the order. Returns the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

slot.description: The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it

moveAfter.description: Put it after this slot (0: first)

page.description: The page to put it on

tools.name: remove_quiz_slot
tools.description: Remove a slot from a quiz, as the edit page's delete icon does; the question stays in its bank. A quiz with attempts can't change its questions. Returns the quiz's structure. Confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

slot.description: The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it

tools.name: set_quiz_pages
tools.description: Set how a quiz's questions are split into pages: perPage questions a page (0 for all on one), as "Repaginate" does, or page breaks exactly after the slots in breaksAfter. Returns the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

perPage.description: Questions per page; 0 for one page

breaksAfter.description: Or: a page break after each of these slots, and nowhere else

tools.name: add_quiz_section
tools.description: Add a section heading to a quiz, starting at a slot (the first of its page: see set_quiz_pages), optionally shuffling its questions. Returns the new section's id and the quiz's structure. Changes the quiz: confirm with the person first.

quizId.description: The quiz's id (course module id), as get_course_structure gives it

firstSlot.description: The slot's place in the quiz, from 1, as get_quiz_structure gives it

tools.name: get_gradebook_setup
tools.description: Read how a course's grades are computed, as the gradebook setup page shows it: its categories (aggregation, weight, maximum) and grade items (category, maximum, weight). No one's grades.

tools.name: update_grade_item
tools.description: Change a grade item from get_gradebook_setup: move it into a category, set its weight (percent, overriding the automatic one) or a manual item's maximum grade (an activity's is set in the activity). Returns the item afterwards. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

category.description: The category to move it into

tools.name: add_grade_category
tools.description: Add a grade category to a course's gradebook, at the top level or inside another, with its aggregation. Returns it as the setup shows it. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

parentId.description: The category to put it in; the course's top level when missing

tools.name: add_grade_item
tools.description: Add a grade item graded in the gradebook (not by an activity): out of maxGrade (Moodle's default 100) or on a scale, at the top level or in a category, optionally hidden from students. Returns it as the setup shows it. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

categoryId.description: The category to put it in, as get_gradebook_setup gives it

tools.name: update_grade_category
tools.description: Change a grade category from get_gradebook_setup: its name, aggregation, weight in its parent (percent, overriding the automatic one), or move it into another category. Returns it afterwards. Changes how grades are computed: confirm with the person first.

parentId.description: The category to move it into

tools.name: delete_grade_category
tools.description: Delete a grade category: Moodle moves what it held into its parent and deletes its total's grades; the course's own category can't be deleted. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: delete_grade_item
tools.description: Delete a manual grade item and every grade in it. An activity's item goes with its activity, so it's refused. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List the upcoming events of the person's calendar, as its "Upcoming events" view does, in one course or in all: course events, activities' dates and the person's own events.

courseId.description: Only this course's; every course when missing

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create an event in a course's calendar, which its participants see: a name, a start (ISO 8601 with its time zone), and optionally a duration and a description (HTML). Returns the event. Visible to the course: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete a calendar event the person can manage (a course event, or their own), by its id from list_events or create_event. Activities' dates are changed in the activity instead. Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Read one calendar event by its id, as list_events gives them.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Change a calendar event through the calendar's own form: only what's given changes; a new start keeps its length unless a new one is given. Activities' dates are changed in the activity instead. Returns the event afterwards. Visible to the course: confirm with the person first.

wholeSeries.description: For a repeated event: change every one

tools.name: show_browser
tools.description: Show the browser to the person, so they can watch what the tools do: the window opens now (the session is kept) and each tool brings the Moodle page it works on to the front. Or hide it again: the window closes and tools go on without one. Only when the person asks to watch or to stop watching. Open tabs don't survive the switch; what was saved in Moodle does. Changes nothing in Moodle.

visible.description: true to show the browser and follow the tools in it, false to hide it

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Open a page of the configured Moodle site in the browser tools' tab: a URL of the site, or a path relative to it. Other sites are refused. A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it. Works in one tab of the server's session (the one show_browser displays; Moodle tools may move it while the browser is shown).

url.description: A URL of the site, or a path relative to it (course/view.php?id=3)

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: The page in the browser tools' tab as an accessibility tree (roles, names, values), with a ref per element ([ref=e12]) for the other browser tools. By default the main region only (#region-main, where Moodle puts the content), or the whole page, or one element's subtree by ref. Cut at 30000 characters: snapshot a narrower part when cut. A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

scope.description: "main" (default): Moodle's main region; "page": everything, navigation included

ref.description: Only this element's subtree (from a previous snapshot)

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element of the browser tools' tab by its snapshot ref (a link, button, checkbox, tab…), and wait for the page it leads to. Links to other sites are blocked. A click can change the site (save, delete, submit): confirm with the person first, as with any Moodle change. A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

ref.description: The element's ref from the latest browser_snapshot, like e12

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Fill a text field of the browser tools' tab by its snapshot ref, replacing what it holds; optionally press Enter after. Password fields are refused: the person logs in themselves (login). A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

ref.description: The element's ref from the latest browser_snapshot, like e12

tools.name: browser_select
tools.description: Choose options in a select of the browser tools' tab by its snapshot ref, by their values or visible labels (several for a multiple select). A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

ref.description: The element's ref from the latest browser_snapshot, like e12

tools.name: browser_upload
tools.description: Set local files on a file input of the browser tools' tab by its snapshot ref (in Moodle's file picker, the "Upload a file" input), as if the person had chosen them. Absolute paths. A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

ref.description: The element's ref from the latest browser_snapshot, like e12

tools.name: browser_wait
tools.description: Wait in the browser tools' tab until a text shows, until it's gone (in the page or any frame in it, such as a SCORM package's), or for some seconds (at most 30): for pages that load or change on their own. A fallback: use it only when no Moodle tool covers the task, and say which task, so a tool can be made for it.

textGone.description: Wait until this text is gone

seconds.description: Wait this long (with a text: the most to wait; default 10)

tools.name: server_info
tools.description: Show this server's version and effective configuration: the active Moodle site and the others, the browser profile folder, the browser, and where each setting came from. Contains no secrets. Does not open the browser.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the Moodle sites this server knows, by name: their URL, which one is active (every other tool works on it) and whether each comes from the person's configuration or was added at run time. Switch with use_site.

tools.name: add_site
tools.description: Add a Moodle site to this server, kept for later sessions: its URL (any page of it works) and, optionally, a short name (letters, digits, dots, hyphens; its host by default). Without url, the person is asked for both in their app, where the client can ask them (MCP elicitation); else ask them yourself. Two accounts on one site are two sites: add the second with a name of its own. It doesn't become active: switch to it with use_site, and log in there when a tool asks. Only when the person asks for another site.

url.description: The site's URL, or any page of it; without it, the person is asked in their app when it can

name.description: A short name for it; its host by default

tools.name: use_site
tools.description: Make another known site the active one, by name (list_sites): every other tool works on it from now on. The previous site's browser closes and keeps its session; if the new one has none, the next tool asks to log in. Tell the person which site you're now working on. Lasts for this session.

name.description: The site's name, as list_sites gives it

tools.name: remove_site
tools.description: Forget a site added at run time, by name, and delete its browser profile with its session. Not the active site (switch first) nor one from the person's configuration (they remove it there). Can't be undone: confirm with the person first.

name.description: The site's name, as list_sites gives it

tools.name: copy_between_sites
tools.description: Copy a course's content from one of this server's sites to another (list_sites): some activities (activityIds), some sections with everything in them (sectionIds), or, with neither, the whole course. Through Moodle's backup on the first site and its restore on the second, never with people's data and naming no one; the file stays on this computer, never passes through you, and is deleted after. It goes into an existing course (toCourseId): at the end of one of its sections (toSectionId), or, for sections, as new ones after toAfterSectionId; a whole course can go into a new course in a category instead (toCategoryId). Returns what was created, and warnings for what was left broken (restrictions or links to what wasn't copied) for the person to fix. Each site needs a session (use_site, then login). The active site stays the same. Within one site, use import_activities or copy_course. It can take minutes. Changes the target site: confirm with the person first.

fromSite.description: A site's name, as list_sites gives it

courseId.description: The course to copy from, on fromSite

activityIds.description: Only these activities and resources, by course module id

sectionIds.description: Only these sections, by id, each with everything in it

toSite.description: A site's name, as list_sites gives it

toCourseId.description: An existing course on toSite to copy into

toSectionId.description: Into toCourseId: every copied activity at the end of this section

toAfterSectionId.description: Into toCourseId: copied sections as new sections after this one

toCategoryId.description: A whole course only: a new course in this category on toSite, instead of toCourseId

instructions:
This server works a Moodle site through a real browser, logged in as the person using it.

- When a tool says the server has no Moodle site yet, call configure with the site URL from your own configuration, or ask the person for it. configure also sets the browser profile folder and headless mode; it lasts for this session only.
- Each tool is a Moodle task (list courses, list assignments, read submissions...): use them first. Only when none covers the task, use the browser_* tools (navigate, snapshot, click, type, select, upload, screenshot, wait) on the site, and tell the person which task needed them. Clicks can change the site: confirm with the person first.
- When the person asks to watch what you do in Moodle, call show_browser with visible true: a window opens and follows each tool's page. When they ask to stop watching, call it with false. Don't call it otherwise.
- The server never handles passwords. When a tool reports that the session is missing or expired, call login: it opens a browser window where the person logs in themselves, and waits for them. Tell the person to look for that window. Never ask the person for their password.
- Tools annotated read-only only read. Any tool that changes the site says so in its annotations and description; confirm with the person before calling one.
- Moodle pages can be slow: prefer one tool call that returns what you need over many small ones.
- When a tool says the server is downloading a browser (no Edge or Chrome on the machine), tell the person and retry after a minute or two.
- Other people may reach you as aliases (A-7KQ2XM): the server pseudonymizes them, and names, emails and other personal data in their texts become aliases or placeholders. Use the aliases as given, also to act on someone (grade_submission takes user). Never try to find out who an alias is: the person resolves aliases on their own machine. Text you write to Moodle (feedback, posts) is refused if it holds an alias, because people would read it as is: address the student as "you" instead.
- The server may know several Moodle sites (list_sites); every tool works on the active one. When the person means another site, switch with use_site and say which one you're working on.
- server_info shows the effective configuration (site, profile folder, browser, scopes, student data), useful when something fails.
